blocks.text: 1. Embedding Cache

blocks.alt: Text is checked against an embedding cache for whether it is already embedded

blocks.text: Caching named what specifically to cache in a RAG pipeline, pointing to embedding cache and response cache as the two most impactful places to apply it. Embedding Cache, storing computed embeddings so the same text never gets embedded twice, is the first of those two concrete applications.
It keys a cache by the exact text content, reusing the stored vector on any exact repeat.
2. Embedding Is Expensive And Deterministic
Running a real embedding model costs real compute per call.
The exact same input text always produces the exact same embedding vector from a fixed model.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Property","Why it enables caching"],"rows":[["Deterministic","Same text and model always produce the same vector"],["Expensive","Every call costs real compute worth avoiding on repeats"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Caching Query Embeddings Versus Chunk Embeddings

blocks.alt: A query embedding cache is compared against a chunk embedding cache

blocks.text: Chunk embeddings are typically computed once at ingestion, while query embeddings repeat across many user sessions.
Query embedding caching is where the recurring compute savings actually accumulate.
4. The Cache Key Must Include The Model Version

blocks.alt: Text plus model version forms the cache key

blocks.text: Two different embedding models produce different vectors for the exact same text.
The cache key must include which model produced the vector, not just the text alone.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A cache key built from only the query text, would incorrectly return a vector from an older embedding model after an upgrade, unless the model identifier is also part of the key.
blocks.text: A cache key built from only the query text would incorrectly return a vector from an older embedding model after an upgrade, unless the model identifier is also part of the key.
5. Near-Duplicate Queries Still Miss The Exact Cache

blocks.alt: Two near-identical queries produce different cache keys

blocks.text: As with one query misses different things than many in Fusion RAG, two queries with the exact same meaning but different wording still produce two different cache keys.
An exact-match embedding cache misses this near-duplicate case entirely.

blocks.text: 6. Invalidating The Embedding Cache On Model Change

blocks.alt: A model upgrade invalidates the entire cache

blocks.text: Upgrading to a new embedding model makes every previously cached vector wrong for that model.
The entire embedding cache needs invalidating on any model change, not just individual entries.
7. Embedding Cache Reduces Latency, Not Just Cost

blocks.alt: An embedding cache reduces both latency and cost

blocks.text: As with reasoning token cost in Chain Of Thought, a cached embedding lookup is far faster than a real embedding model call.
Embedding caching cuts response latency, not just compute spend.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A cache lookup completing in milliseconds versus a real embedding model call taking far longer means embedding caching improves the user-facing response time directly, beyond simply lowering compute bills.

blocks.text: 8. Storing Embedding Caches At Scale
A production embedding cache typically lives in a fast key-value store separate from the main vector database.
A real infrastructure choice distinct from where the actual document embeddings are indexed.
9. Recognizing When An Embedding Cache Earns Its Infrastructure

blocks.alt: Repeated queries or chunks point toward using an embedding cache

blocks.text: A system serving repeated or similar queries benefits from an embedding cache.
A system where every query is unique gets little benefit from caching embeddings.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates an embedding cache keyed by text and model version, with cache hits, misses, and a full invalidation on model upgrade.

code.content:
embedding_cache = {}

def embed(text, model_version):
    # simulated expensive embedding call
    return [hash(text + model_version) % 100 for _ in range(3)]

def cached_embed(text, model_version):
    # the cache key must include the model version
    cache_key = (text.strip().lower(), model_version)
    if cache_key in embedding_cache:
        return "hit", embedding_cache[cache_key]
    vector = embed(text, model_version)
    embedding_cache[cache_key] = vector
    return "miss", vector

def invalidate_cache_for_model(old_model_version):
    # invalidating the embedding cache on model change
    keys_to_remove = [k for k in embedding_cache if k[1] == old_model_version]
    for k in keys_to_remove:
        del embedding_cache[k]
    return len(keys_to_remove)

status, vector = cached_embed("What does the Falcon plan cost?", "v1")
print(f"First call: {status}")

status, vector = cached_embed("What does the Falcon plan cost?", "v1")
print(f"Repeat call: {status}")

removed = invalidate_cache_for_model("v1")
print(f"\nInvalidated {removed} entries after model upgrade")

status, vector = cached_embed("What does the Falcon plan cost?", "v1")
print(f"Call after invalidation: {status}")

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Running this example shows the repeat call hitting the cache while the call after model invalidation misses again, exactly the model-version-aware caching and invalidation.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Keying the embedding cache by text alone, ignoring which model produced the vector.
Assuming near-duplicate queries will hit the cache when only exact text matches will.
Upgrading the embedding model without invalidating the entire existing cache.
Treating embedding caching as only a cost optimization, missing its latency benefit.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: An embedding cache stores computed embeddings so the same text never gets embedded twice.
Embedding is expensive and deterministic, making it well suited to caching.
Query embeddings repeat across sessions far more than chunk embeddings, making them the bigger win.
The cache key must include the model version, since different models produce different vectors.
Near-duplicate queries with different wording still miss an exact-match embedding cache.
Upgrading the embedding model requires invalidating the entire cache, not just individual entries.
A cached embedding lookup is far faster than a real model call, cutting latency, not just cost.
A production embedding cache typically lives in a fast key-value store, separate from the vector database.
